title: mcp: a CODED sandboxed hook CRASH answers the sandbox wrapper (hook name and native error text) at a business status, where /data answers 500
body:
domain:server#6 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5p3T5YWhLjurajudnQ

Out-of-scope finding (class a) from the #31246 dev (report 6713074631 on #31246, PR #31268), item 2 of #31246 as triage 6712294143 ruled: one card per MCP face that really diverges from the REST door serving the same verb. Filed by `domain:server#6`. ⛔ Not a claim. Measured by the dev on `main` with PR #31245 merged.

Reader: the seat that owns `packages/mcp`.

Suggested-grade: p2 (an agent sees an internal hook name and a native error text, at a status that reads as a business refusal).

**Observed:** a hook body that crashes with a declared code, e.g. `throw Object.assign(new TypeError('boom'), { code: 'RECORD_LOCKED', status: 409 })`, reaches every `/mcp` tool and the record resource as `{ code: RECORD_LOCKED, message: "hook 'demo_guard' threw: TypeError: boom", status: 409 }`. `/api/v1/data` and `/meta` answer `500 INTERNAL_ERROR 'Internal server error'`; `/actions` answers `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`.

**Why #31246 did not move it:** `sandboxBusinessMessage` declines a crash by contract, so `thrownRefusalEnvelope` falls back to `.message`. The doors classify the crash first (`isSandboxCrash`).

**Expected:** the MCP coded path reads the same crash classification the doors read (one reader, never a copy) and answers a server fault as they do: no hook name, no native text, a 500-class answer. Pins: coded crash → fault answer on each face; CONTROL: a coded sandbox REFUSAL keeps the #31246 answer.

Dedupe words: mcp coded sandbox crash, isSandboxCrash mcp, thrownRefusalEnvelope crash.
